target.title: fix(copilot): clean up polling abort listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where GitHub Copilot device-code OAuth polling would leave abort listeners on a shared `AbortSignal` after each successful sleep. `once: true` only removes the listener when abort fires, so normal multi-round `authorization_pending` polling accumulates closures and can trigger EventTarget listener leak warnings.

## Why This Change Was Made

`abortableSleep` in the Copilot OAuth helper now settles once on either timer resolve or abort: clear the timer, remove the named `onAbort` listener, then resolve/reject. Already-aborted signals reject immediately without registering a listener. Polling intervals and error text are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** Each successful poll sleep left an abort listener on the login cancel signal.
**After:** Resolve and abort both release the timer/listener; cancel still surfaces as `Login cancelled`.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/copilot-poll-listener-cleanup` | Base: `upstream/main` | Head: `d506c35a6c87` | Node: v24.18.0 — Windows

### Regression tests

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > does not accumulate abort listeners across authorization_pending rounds
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > removes the abort listener when cancelled during sleep
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > rejects an already-aborted signal without registering a listener
```

### Diff summary

```text
src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts       | settle-once cleanup for abortableSleep
src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts  | fake-timer polling listener regressions
```

What was not tested: completing a full interactive browser authorization to obtain a live Copilot access token.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Copilot OAuth poll sleeps no longer accumulate abort listeners on a shared cancel signal after normal (non-abort) wakeups; cancellation during polling still rejects with `Login cancelled` and releases listeners.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, patched branch `d506c35a6c87`; production `testing.pollForGitHubAccessToken` / `testing.startDeviceFlow` imported from source via `node --import tsx --trace-warnings`.
**Steps run after the patch:**

1. Import production `testing.pollForGitHubAccessToken` from `src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts` and run multi-round `authorization_pending` polling with **real timers** (80 ms interval), sampling `getEventListeners(signal, "abort")` during the run.
2. Abort during an in-flight poll sleep (2 s interval, abort at 30 ms) and assert listener count returns to 0 with `Login cancelled`.
3. Start a **live** `testing.startDeviceFlow("github.com")`, poll with the returned device code until `authorization_pending`, abort during the real interval, and capture warning diagnostics (`--trace-warnings` + `process.on("warning")`).

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings --trace-warnings -e "<import production testing.* from github-copilot.ts>"

{
  "stubbed": {
    "token": "proof-redacted",
    "peak": 1,
    "final": 0
  },
  "cancel": {
    "before": 1,
    "msg": "Login cancelled",
    "final": 0
  },
  "live": {
    "verificationUri": "https://github.com/login/device",
    "userCodeRedacted": "C1**",
    "intervalMs": 5000,
    "abortAfterMs": 5200,
    "peak": 1,
    "final": 0,
    "cancelMessage": "Login cancelled"
  },
  "warnings": [],
  "warningsEmpty": true
}
```

**Observed result:** Across stubbed multi-round polling and a live github.com device-code pending poll, peak active abort listeners never exceeded 1 and final listener count returned to 0 after each successful sleep and after cancel; `--trace-warnings` captured no EventTarget/listener warnings.
**Not tested:** Completing browser authorization to exchange the live device code for a Copilot access token; full `loginGitHubCopilot` UI prompt path.

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
